thread:
alex: FYI I pulled a 1h flame on the host proxy during the KV-cache incident yesterday, and tokenization is eating ~27% of CPU on p3-small hosts. noticed a lot of tiny grpc frames too.
jia: ugh. is that the python tokenizer threadpool or the per-request tokenize call?
alex: per-request (fastapi endpoint) -> sync tokenize -> writes to uvloop worker. We get small gen_chunks of ~128 bytes from the client, grpc->http2 flow control causes lots of syscalls. stack trace snip:
```
# host proc top
PID  USER      %CPU %MEM    VSZ   RSS TTY      STAT START   TIME COMMAND
3245 root      32.7  1.1  123456 23456 ?       Ssl  09:12   0:32 python /srv/host-proxy/main.py
```
morgan: can you paste the grpc log? small frames point to streaming chunking on the client side, maybe JS SDK is sending per-keystroke.
alex: sending excerpt:
```
I2026-03-17T09:14:12Z grpc: recv WINDOW_UPDATE stream 1 size 65535
I2026-03-17T09:14:12Z http: read 64 bytes -> parse -> dispatch
```
oscar: two immediate things: 1) batch tokenization across requests when they arrive within 3ms window, 2) coalesce tiny http chunks at ingress before parsing. both should cut syscall churn.
jia: agreed. batching needs to be careful: kernel selection for small batches picks fp16 kernels that are suboptimal for short sequences. we should gate batcher to prefer single-request fast-path when seq_len < 32.
perf-bot: perf-alert: host-proxy:tokenize_cpu spike +27% at 2026-03-17T09:13:50Z; p99 latency +120ms
morgan: also KV cache eviction pattern looked like this: when batches coalesce, they serialize KV warmups together which causes a sudden memory pressure and thrash. when cache misses hit, decode latency jumps.
alex: exact. trace snippet shows back-to-back kv_loads from same model ID causing liveness churn. Suggestion: add a tiny jitter into kvcache fetch scheduling and ensure hot-key pinning for rolling windows.
oscar: quick patch plan:
- coalesce ingress byte chunks into 8k buffer in host-proxy (C ext) before parse
- introduce a 3ms micro-batcher for tokenization (python worker pool) with a fast path for seq_len<32 bypass
- kvcache: add fetch jitter + per-host hot key pinning
- metric: add tag kvcache.hit_group so we can break down bursts
jia: can we also switch grpc server read to use readv and reduce copies? should be ~15% less CPU.
morgan: test matrix: run with 10k rps synthetic with short sequences, compare p50/p99 and cpu. I can set up perf harness today.
alex: I'll prototype coalescer in C and the micro-batcher. aiming for canary tomorrow.
jia: thanks. tagging @eng-oncall in case rollouts touch proxies :eng-oncall:
morgan: noted. also recording this thread to perf doc.
alex: thanks all :thumbsup:"
